landmark_fixes.change: Not mustard yellow. Five storeys, flat roof covered in solar panels. Facade in alternating vertical bays: terracotta/rust-brown panel bays (#b4643c) at both ends and two in the middle, white (#eeeeea) and warm grey-taupe (#9a948a) bays between, a pale blue-grey (#a9b6c0) end wall facing the river; every bay has stacked balconies with dark rails. street_feel: Red Shores at night is the brightest thing on the east side: light poles round the oval, the grandstand glass lit, and in Gold Cup week (mid-August) a crowd ten deep against the white rail with the Ferris wheel lit up behind the south turn. The rest of the year the event grounds are an empty asphalt lot with light poles.

Old Home Week (mid-August): the midway fills the Eastlink and event-grounds lots right up to the track - Ferris wheel, striped tents, ticket booths, red-and-white pennant strings, lawn chairs along a white pipe rail at the turn; livestock and the show ring inside the Eastlink trade centre with an 'OLD HOME WEEK' banner on the boards.

Kensington Road past the arena: navy metal box on red brick, a new sidewalk (2019) on the arena side with wooden utility poles and a few street trees; people used to walk in the road because Atlantic Lotto fenced off the loading zone between the arena and the casino.

The Riverside/Grafton/bridge corner (rebuilt 2024): a free-flow lane from Grafton onto the bridge, red shale shoulders, cobra-head lights, a curved berm of blue spruce, the white Irving tanks behind chain-link across the road from the Tim's and Wendy's. Tim's drive-thru line backs up onto the lot at 8 a.m.

Hillsborough Park: 1970s bungalows with concrete curbs and sidewalks, bare maples, wide driveways; the pickleball courts are the busiest thing in the neighbourhood, with paddles lined up on the fence. A fenced (1.2 m galvanized chain-link, double gate) off-leash dog park off Acadian Drive near the QEH, a field edged by spruce woods - not placed because Acadian Drive and the dog park aren't in the map data.

East Royalty District Park is on the old sewage lagoon between Robertson Road and Bonnie Blink Drive; the city approved about $500k (2025) for paths, parking, a multi-use sports pad, a pump track loop, picnic areas and a floating boardwalk on Wright's Creek over about five years - only the playground and paths are there now.

Community mailboxes are on nearly every newer East Royalty and Stratford street: grey banks with red tops on a paver pad at a corner, usually with a 'Save door-to-door' sign long gone. In winter the locks freeze (CBC ran that story twice).

Stratford from the bridge: the welcome sign, then a wide mown field down to the red bank and the new grey boardwalk curving along the cove to the Michael Thomas circle, with Shorefront's rust-and-white block behind and downtown Charlottetown across the water. Behind the road: gas bars, Burger King, the Bunbury Mall lot.

Glen Stewart Primary's yard is big and open: five separate play areas on gravel or black rubber, each edged with timbers, primary-coloured structures, blue swing sets and benches, basketball hoops, a natural playground (log steps and a green slide on a mound) by the spruce woods.

Off the map to the east (no entries): Stratford Town Centre (Shakespeare Drive), Mason Road's commercial strip, Robert Cotton Park (only its western trail end is inside the map) and the Bunbury Road youth-centre crosswalk.
